correctness.rationale: Piecewise uniform survival integration gives the exact cubic. Its discriminant is \(3b^2(b-1)^6Q(b)\); one-positive-root Descartes analysis of \(Q(1+t)\) and endpoint signs establish all root counts. A positive witness at \(b=5\) fixes root locations, and double-root Taylor analysis gives the sharp square-root onset. The \(10W_1\) stability bound proves smooth persistence. U-statistic projection and null variance \(4/5\) establish positive alternative variance and two nonunit limiting rejection rates. The bundled standalone checker executed 69 independent algebraic/numeric assertions, supplementing rather than replacing the proof.

value.rationale: A sharp natural mixing-ratio threshold identifies when heterogeneity between two individually negative-scoring lifetime cohorts produces positive contrast and precisely two distinct blind alternatives; the phenomenon persists under smooth strictly positive perturbations. This is a complete sign/zero classification of an interpretable model, and its nonunit limiting rejection probabilities delimit legitimate applications of a signed test without impugning the original restricted one-sided consistency theorem. The threshold and two branches are structurally motivated, not arbitrary parameter substitutions or a null-table recomputation.
